# Set Position

Moves selected splats, points or mesh vertices to new positions with an optional offset.

`lfs.set_position` · Geometry

## How to use

Connect Position to Position, then set Offset for a relative move.  
Without that connection, Position defaults to the origin.  

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Geometry | `Geometry` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Geometry you want to edit. Connect a source; an unconnected input supplies no geometry. |
| Selection | `Selection` | lfs.float | 1 | min 0; max 1; step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Where you apply the edit, 0–1: 0 leaves it unchanged, 1 applies it fully. Unconnected means everything. |
| Position | `Position` | lfs.vector | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | New position in local scene units. The default is the origin; connect Position to retain existing positions. |
| Offset | `Offset` | lfs.vector | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Extra movement along X, Y and Z in local scene units. (0, 0, 0), the default, adds no movement. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Geometry | `Geometry` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Resulting geometry. Connect to another editing node or Group Output. |
